requirements.text: One small closable PETG enclosure accepts interchangeable separately printed TPU liners and a loose metal nut.

provenance.statement: User requests one small PETG exterior, closable, with TPU inserts and space to shake a stock metal nut.

requirements.text: The floor, ceiling and all four interior walls have TPU damping coverage.

provenance.statement: User explicitly requires damping on the bottom, top, and all four walls.

requirements.text: All object-contact interior faces are flat; damping structures are inside the liner.

provenance.statement: User clarification: the interior needs to be flat for the objects, while the liner may have structures inside.

questions.criterion: The coupon contact field is flat and free of lettering/protrusions.

requirements.text: Several permanently labeled CAD-defined internal damping configurations can be printed together.

provenance.statement: User asks for labeled variants, explicit CAD structures rather than infill, and a batch print; additional variants are welcome.

questions.criterion: Eight named plate placements include permanent recessed IDs outside test fields.

requirements.text: Use research to inform a reusable damping experiment and compare variants by shaking the same metal nut.

provenance.statement: User requests research on effective damping structures and plans to report which liner performs best.

requirements.text: Prioritize maximum quietness in a thin liner and recommend a focused print batch with a solid control and the most promising candidates.

provenance.statement: User follow-up: maximize quietness while keeping it thin; provide a STEP set focused on more confident candidates and retain control A.

requirements.text: Thinner follow-up liners retain both continuous inner and outer TPU skins for stable printing.

provenance.statement: User reports I10 shell-side print damage, says both walls are needed, and requests one or two significantly thinner stable variants; slicer changes are allowed.

questions.criterion: The coupon retains both full continuous skins.

requirements.text: Provide roughly 30 mm square flat plate samples, four to eight designs printable together, with filled exterior edges.

provenance.statement: User requests four to eight roughly three-centimetre square bottom-plate samples rather than full boxes, filled exterior overhangs and a flat test face.

questions.criterion: Eight separate 30 mm plates have filled edges, planar fields, recessed IDs and the declared skin/core geometry.

requirements.text: Explore structures that reduce visible surface lines and waviness beyond the current 50% ironing result.

provenance.statement: User reports visible surface waviness despite improvement at 50% ironing and requests several internal structure experiments.

questions.criterion: User compares identical-process coupons to F0 and F7 for reduced rib print-through, flatness and visible lines.

requirements.text: Keep damping usefulness as a later physical test; S16 remains the preferred baseline.

provenance.statement: User names S16 as the best so far and says damping must still be tested later while initially focusing on surface texture.

questions.criterion: A later controlled physical comparison tests damping; no geometric proxy qualifies quietness.

evidence.summary: Existing assertion group passed; see linked criteria/limits

decisions.text: 30 mm plates, 1.2 mm frame, 10 mm solid label band, backing down; CAD cores remain empty with 100% material fill. Solid F7 is a deliberate control.

hypotheses.text: F3: straight, 0.4 mm skin, 3.2 mm pitch. Thicker skins and closer supports may flatten the surface while increasing stiffness. Retained air is not acoustic evidence.
